supersessionNote: The admission/page-budget observations remain valid. Dedicated Root Port runs later completed 32G and 64G EFI guest runtime.

environment.outerVmm: QEMU 6.2.0 q35/KVM with virtual Intel IOMMU
environment.endpoint: QEMU pci-testdev 1b36:0005 with a no-backing 64-bit prefetchable BAR

notes: pciPassthru.64bitMMIOSizeGB is ignored when pciPassthru.use64bitMMIO is absent or FALSE.
TRUE opens the large-MMIO path and uses an observable 32 GiB default budget when SizeGB is absent.
An explicitly undersized SizeGB replaces that 32 GiB component; it is not rounded up to fit the BAR.

inference: A 32 GiB no-backing BAR fits the TRUE-only default mapping budget, while a 64 GiB BAR does not.
A 64 GiB BAR maps only when both the TRUE gate and SizeGB=64 are present in this build.
The test removes sparse-file or shared-memory capacity as an explanation because pci-testdev reports the BAR without allocating equal-sized backing storage.
The nested EFI guest did not reach its heartbeat after successful 32/64 GiB mappings, so these are admission and IOMMU-mapping conclusions, not guest-runtime support claims.
The outer QEMU platform also needed both a 64 GiB q35 hole64 and a matching OVMF aperture before ESXi itself could boot with the 64 GiB endpoint.
